newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian Rigas Kommerc Banka gets Thomson rating.
newsitem.headline: Latvian Rigas Kommerc Banka gets Thomson rating.

text.p: One of Latvia's leading commercial banks, Rigas Kommerc Banka (RKB), said on Tuesday that it has received the first rating for a Latvian bank by Thomson Bankwatch.
The bank said in a statement that Thomson gave it a long-term rating of BB-, a short-term rating of LC-2 and an intra-country issuer rating of IC-C.

"The ratings reflect the financial stability of the bank as a whole, its position and competitivity on the market and also the security of long and short-term (up to one year) deposits in Rigas Kommerc Banka," the bank said.
RKB is the third-largest Latvian bank and recently concluded a deal whereby the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) bought some 23 percent of its shares.
RKB quoted Thomson as saying that it gave the bank the BB- long-term rating as it was the oldest commercial bank in Latvia, which continued to develop as a universal bank.
It noted that although 1995 had been a difficult year, RKB kept its place as one of the most trusted banks in Latvia.
Latvia was in mid-1995 hit by one of the worst banking crises in eastern Europe but has recovered well.
Thomson said it gave the short-term and intra-country issuer rating based on the conservatism of the bank and its stable financial position.
The rating agency added that in its opinion the bank would develop as one of the main commercial banks in Latvia and that its new shareholders would help in its further development.
